chunks.title: FAQ: Is it expensive to study in China?
chunks.text: Q: Is it expensive to study in China? A: No. China is one of the most affordable study destinations. Tuition is low compared to Western countries, and many students study on full or partial scholarships such as CSC, which can cover tuition, accommodation and a monthly stipend.

chunks.title: FAQ: Do I need to know Chinese to study in China?
chunks.text: Q: Do I need to know Chinese to study in China? A: Not always. 60 of the 72 programmes in our current list are taught in English. Chinese-taught programmes ask for an HSK certificate (usually HSK 4 or 5) - and we help you prepare. Basic Chinese still makes daily life much easier.

chunks.title: FAQ: What scholarships can IFFI Consultant help me apply for?
chunks.text: Q: What scholarships can IFFI Consultant help me apply for? A: We assist with the Chinese Government Scholarship (CSC), Confucius Institute Scholarship, provincial scholarships and individual university scholarships, depending on your profile and programme.

chunks.title: FAQ: How long does the admission process take?
chunks.text: Q: How long does the admission process take? A: It varies by university and intake, but typically the admission process takes 4-10 weeks. Most September-intake deadlines in our list fall in May and June, so applying early is very important.

chunks.title: FAQ: Which documents do I need to apply?
chunks.text: Q: Which documents do I need to apply? A: Generally: passport (valid 2+ years), academic certificates and transcripts, a study plan or personal statement, recommendation letters, a medical examination form, a police character certificate and passport-size photos. We give you a personalised checklist.

chunks.title: FAQ: Is studying in China safe for international students?
chunks.text: Q: Is studying in China safe for international students? A: Yes. China is considered very safe, with modern campuses, good public transport and large, welcoming international student communities in most major cities.

chunks.title: CSC Scholarship: A Complete Step-by-Step Guide - Introduction
chunks.text: CSC Scholarship: A Complete Step-by-Step Guide. The CSC (Chinese Government Scholarship) is one of the most sought-after fully-funded scholarships. It can cover tuition, accommodation, monthly stipend and medical insurance. It is competitive, so a complete, well-prepared file matters. This guide walks through how it works and how to prepare.

chunks.title: CSC Scholarship: A Complete Step-by-Step Guide - What the CSC scholarship covers
chunks.text: CSC Scholarship: A Complete Step-by-Step Guide. What the CSC scholarship covers A full CSC award usually covers tuition, on-campus accommodation, comprehensive medical insurance and a monthly living allowance. The allowance depends on your level. In our current list, fully funded Master offers pay up to 3,000 CNY a month and PhD offers 3,500 CNY a month.

chunks.title: CSC Scholarship: A Complete Step-by-Step Guide - Type A and Type B
chunks.text: CSC Scholarship: A Complete Step-by-Step Guide. Type A and Type B Type A (bilateral programme): you apply through the Chinese embassy or the education authority in your home country, which nominates candidates. Places per country are limited. Type B (Chinese University Program): you apply directly to a designated Chinese university, which selects and nominates you. This is the route most of our students use. For Type B, the CSC online application asks for the agency number of the university you are applying to. Each university has its own number. Using the wrong one sends your file to the wrong place, so ask us for the correct agency number before you submit.

chunks.title: CSC Scholarship: A Complete Step-by-Step Guide - Who is eligible
chunks.text: CSC Scholarship: A Complete Step-by-Step Guide. Who is eligible Bachelor: Completed (or final year of) 12 years of school - FSc, A-Level, HSC or equivalent. Master: Completed Bachelor's degree. PhD: Completed Master's degree. Good health and a clean police record. English (or Chinese) proficiency for the programme you choose. Many universities accept IELTS, TOEFL or Duolingo; some run their own test. There is no single cut-off mark. Universities look at your whole file: grades, study plan, recommendation letters and timing. Try our scholarship eligibility checker to see where you stand.

chunks.text: CSC Scholarship: A Complete Step-by-Step Guide. chunks.text: CSC Scholarship: A Complete Step-by-Step Guide. When to apply Scholarship applications for the September intake open several months in advance. Start preparing documents in the autumn before you want to travel.

chunks.text: CSC Scholarship: A Complete Step-by-Step Guide. chunks.text: How to Apply for a Chinese Student Visa in 2026. A Chinese student visa is one of the most important requirements for studying in China. Students generally need an admission letter, JW202/JW201 form, passport, photographs, medical documents, and other supporting paperwork. The process includes receiving admission confirmation from the university, preparing the required documents, submitting the visa application, and attending any necessary verification procedures.

chunks.title: How to Apply for a Chinese Student Visa in 2026 - Step 1: Receive your admission documents
chunks.text: How to Apply for a Chinese Student Visa in 2026. Step 1: Receive your admission documents After you accept your offer, the university sends your admission letter and a visa application form for study in China : the JW202 for self-funded and university-scholarship students, or the JW201 for Chinese Government Scholarship students. You need the original or the version your university confirms is acceptable.

chunks.title: How to Apply for a Chinese Student Visa in 2026 - Step 2: Prepare your visa file
chunks.text: How to Apply for a Chinese Student Visa in 2026. chunks.title: How to Apply for a Chinese Student Visa in 2026 - Step 3: Submit and collect
chunks.text: How to Apply for a Chinese Student Visa in 2026. Step 3: Submit and collect Submit your file at the Chinese embassy, consulate or visa application service centre that covers your area, and pay the visa fee. Processing usually takes several working days; apply as soon as your documents arrive so you are not rushing before term starts.

chunks.title: How to Apply for a Chinese Student Visa in 2026 - Step 4: After you arrive in China
chunks.text: How to Apply for a Chinese Student Visa in 2026. Step 4: After you arrive in China An X1 visa lets you enter China. Within 30 days of arrival you apply for a student residence permit at the local exit and entry administration, usually with help from your university’s international office. You will often repeat the medical check locally.

chunks.title: How to Apply for a Chinese Student Visa in 2026 - X1 or X2?
chunks.text: How to Apply for a Chinese Student Visa in 2026. X1 or X2? X1 is for study longer than 180 days, which covers degree programmes. X2 is for shorter study such as a one-semester language course. Read X1 vs X2: what you must know for the differences.

chunks.title: How to Apply for a Chinese Student Visa in 2026 - Common mistakes
chunks.text: How to Apply for a Chinese Student Visa in 2026. Common mistakes Booking flights before the visa is issued A medical form that is incomplete or missing the doctor’s stamp Names that do not match exactly across passport, JW form and admission letter Leaving the residence permit until after the 30-day window Visa rules can change. We check your file against the current requirements before you submit.

chunks.title: Choosing a Chinese University in 2026: 985, 211 and Rankings - Introduction
chunks.text: Choosing a Chinese University in 2026: 985, 211 and Rankings. China is home to many globally recognized universities that attract thousands of international students every year. The most famous names are also the hardest to get into and rarely the best value. This guide explains how to read Chinese university labels and rankings, so you can build a shortlist that fits you.

chunks.title: Choosing a Chinese University in 2026: 985, 211 and Rankings - What C9, 985, 211 and Double First-Class mean
chunks.text: Choosing a Chinese University in 2026: 985, 211 and Rankings. What C9, 985, 211 and Double First-Class mean Project 211: a national programme from the 1990s that funded around a hundred leading universities. Project 985: a smaller group within the 211 universities, selected for extra funding to reach world level. C9 League: the nine leading 985 universities, often called China’s Ivy League. Double First-Class: the current national programme that replaced 211 and 985; it recognises whole universities and individual subjects. In our current list, 2 programmes are at 985 universities and 6 are at universities ranked in China’s top 50.

chunks.title: Choosing a Chinese University in 2026: 985, 211 and Rankings - How much rankings matter
chunks.text: Choosing a Chinese University in 2026: 985, 211 and Rankings. How much rankings matter Rankings help, but for most students three other things matter more: whether the programme is taught in English, whether a scholarship makes it affordable, and whether the city fits your budget. A tier-2 city university with a full scholarship often beats a famous name you have to pay for in full.

chunks.title: Top Scholarships for International Students in China - Introduction
chunks.text: Top Scholarships for International Students in China. China offers several scholarships that help international students reduce the cost of education. Popular options include the Chinese Government Scholarship (CSC), provincial scholarships, university scholarships, and Confucius Institute scholarships. These scholarships may cover tuition fees, accommodation, monthly allowances, and medical insurance depending on the program. Students with strong academic records and complete application documents have a higher chance of securing scholarships.

chunks.title: Top Scholarships for International Students in China - 1. Chinese Government Scholarship (CSC)
chunks.text: Top Scholarships for International Students in China. 1. Chinese Government Scholarship (CSC) The best-known award, funded by the Chinese government. A full CSC scholarship covers tuition, accommodation, medical insurance and a monthly stipend. See our complete CSC guide for Type A and Type B.

chunks.title: Top Scholarships for International Students in China - 2. Provincial government scholarships
chunks.text: Top Scholarships for International Students in China. 2. Provincial government scholarships Several provinces fund their own scholarships to attract international students. Programmes in our list mention, for example, a Guangdong Provincial Government Scholarship of 10,000 RMB a year and a Zhejiang Provincial Government Scholarship of 20,000 CNY a year.

chunks.title: Top Scholarships for International Students in China - 3. University scholarships (Type A, B, C)
chunks.text: Top Scholarships for International Students in China. 3. University scholarships (Type A, B, C) Most universities grade their own awards. A typical structure from our brochures: Type A: tuition free, often with free accommodation and sometimes a monthly stipend Type B: tuition free, accommodation paid by the student Type C: part of the tuition waived, for example 50% In our list, 11 Bachelor programmes include a monthly stipend of 417 to 2,000 CNY. The type you receive often depends on your marks and a short interview.

chunks.title: Top Scholarships for International Students in China - 4. Belt and Road and city scholarships
chunks.text: Top Scholarships for International Students in China. 4. Belt and Road and city scholarships Some universities run Belt and Road scholarships for students from partner countries, and some cities add their own awards for excellent students from the second year onwards.

chunks.title: Top Scholarships for International Students in China - 5. Confucius Institute scholarships
chunks.text: Top Scholarships for International Students in China. 5. Confucius Institute scholarships Aimed at students of Chinese language and international Chinese education, from short courses to Master programmes. Useful if you want to build your HSK level first.

chunks.title: Top Scholarships for International Students in China - How to improve your chances
chunks.text: Top Scholarships for International Students in China. How to improve your chances Apply early: many awards are given in order until the quota is used Choose universities where your profile is competitive, not only the most famous ones Write a specific study plan and ask professors who know you for recommendation letters Get your documents attested before the application opens Fully funded offers in our list: 23. Programmes with a tuition-free option: 51. Filter them in the programme finder or check your profile with the eligibility checker .

chunks.title: Why Study in China in 2026? 7 Reasons Students Choose It - Introduction
chunks.text: Why Study in China in 2026? 7 Reasons Students Choose It. China is now home to top-tier universities, affordable tuition, and an unmatched scholarship ecosystem. It also hosts one of the largest international student populations in the world. For students from Pakistan, South Asia, Africa and Central Asia it offers degrees from well-equipped universities at a fraction of Western prices, with generous scholarships on top. Here are the seven reasons we hear most often from the students we counsel, backed by the programmes in our current list.

chunks.title: Why Study in China in 2026? 7 Reasons Students Choose It - 1. Tuition you can actually afford
chunks.text: Why Study in China in 2026? 7 Reasons Students Choose It. 1. Tuition you can actually afford Across the Bachelor programmes in our list, standard tuition ranges from 2,000 to 39,900 CNY a year, with a median of about 14,000 CNY. That is before any scholarship. Use the cost calculator to see these numbers in your own currency.

chunks.title: Why Study in China in 2026? 7 Reasons Students Choose It - 2. Scholarships that cover tuition, housing and a stipend
chunks.text: Why Study in China in 2026? 7 Reasons Students Choose It. 2. Scholarships that cover tuition, housing and a stipend 51 of our 72 programmes have a scholarship option that makes tuition free, and 23 Master and PhD offers are fully funded: free tuition, a free dorm room and a monthly stipend of up to 3,500 CNY. Read our guide to scholarships in China for the details.

chunks.title: Why Study in China in 2026? 7 Reasons Students Choose It - 3. You can study in English
chunks.text: Why Study in China in 2026? 7 Reasons Students Choose It. 3. You can study in English 60 of the 72 programmes in our list are taught in English, including all six MBBS programmes. You do not need to speak Chinese to start, although learning some Mandarin makes daily life much easier.

chunks.title: Why Study in China in 2026? 7 Reasons Students Choose It - 4. Many routes without IELTS
chunks.text: Why Study in China in 2026? 7 Reasons Students Choose It. 4. Many routes without IELTS 7 programmes state clearly that no IELTS or Duolingo score is needed, and another 30 brochures do not mention a language test at all. Some universities run their own short online English test instead. Our eligibility checker shows which programmes fit your English level.

chunks.title: Why Study in China in 2026? 7 Reasons Students Choose It - 5. Modern campuses and strong science and engineering
chunks.text: Why Study in China in 2026? 7 Reasons Students Choose It. 5. Modern campuses and strong science and engineering Chinese universities have invested heavily in laboratories, libraries and housing. Engineering and computing are particularly strong: 43 programmes in our list offer engineering majors and 42 offer computer science or AI.

chunks.title: Why Study in China in 2026? 7 Reasons Students Choose It - 6. Safe cities with large student communities
chunks.text: Why Study in China in 2026? 7 Reasons Students Choose It. 6. Safe cities with large student communities Students consistently describe Chinese cities as safe, with reliable public transport and welcoming international student offices. Most of our programmes are in affordable tier-2 cities in eastern China, such as Nanjing, Hangzhou and Wuhan, rather than the most expensive metropolises.

chunks.title: Why Study in China in 2026? 7 Reasons Students Choose It - 7. A degree that opens doors at home
chunks.text: Why Study in China in 2026? 7 Reasons Students Choose It. 7. A degree that opens doors at home Trade and investment between China and countries such as Pakistan keep growing. Graduates who understand Chinese business culture and speak some Mandarin have an edge with companies working on joint projects, including CPEC.
